summary: Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from circa 1966 to 1976 and later held a post there from circa 1980 to 2018.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982. He studied under Karl Hoffmann, Johanna Narten, and others, later serving as professor at Osaka University and Tohoku University.
Toshihide Unebe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Issai Funahashi. He held a professorship at Doho University, attested in 1991.

Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies who graduated from Keio University. He held posts at Keio University (1937–1981), McGill University (1961, 1969–1975), and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1959–1963), he taught there as a lecturer and held posts at Tokai Gakuin University (~1979–1989) and Shitennoji University (~2011).
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as a professor at Nagoya University from circa 1989 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under supervisors including Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake, as well as Hajime Nakamura.

Toshikazu Watanabe works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015) and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1974–1978). He held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1991–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020).

Toshinori Ochiai specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served at Kacho Junior College (~1989–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019).
Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1929 to 1932. He held posts at Doho University and Otani University (circa 1949–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2009) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2011–2016) and Zhejiang University (~2016–2022).

Toshio Nagahiro worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (1929, 1950–1969), Kyoto University (~1957–1969), and Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).
Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Columbia University. His teachers included Alex Wayman, Yasunori Ejima, and Jikido Takasaki.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Hannan University, the University of Tokyo (circa 1948–1977), and Chuo University (circa 1977–1987).
Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as associate professor at Nagoya University (attested 2006–2011).

Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University under teachers including Enryo Inoue and Seiran Ouchi, later teaching at Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon Universities.

Touhoi Fok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Otani University, later lecturing at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1972–1988).

Touraj Daryaee is a historian specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993–1999) and took a post at the University of California, Irvine, around 2007.

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees at Kyoto University (~1965–1993). He held academic posts at Otemon Gakuin University and Osaka City University (1981–2010), later directing the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).
